What does carpet installation cost in Arlington, WA?

Arlington runs to ramblers, split-levels and newer starter subdivisions, and the math lands in about the same place across all three. One bedroom comes to $600–$1,000; a whole project usually totals $2,400–$3,900. Per square foot, installed, that's $4 to $7 — pad, carpet, labor, new tack strip and haul-away of the old floor all counted. Grade swings the number more than anything else, and that call gets made in your own rooms with the real samples in front of you.
Does the mobile carpet showroom really come out to Arlington?

The nearest showroom is a drive down I-5 to Everett or Lynnwood, so the van comes north instead. It arrives with all three pad grades and 20+ carpet samples, which get spread across the rooms being redone — color reads differently under your own windows than under store lighting. Every room and stair gets measured, you keep a written price before we pull out, and the visit costs nothing.
What does it cost to stretch carpet in Arlington?

Most rooms land between $99 and $180, and $99 per room is the floor. A power stretcher takes the slack out — hallway ripples, the wave in front of a slider — for about a fifth of the cost of replacing it. On original carpet in a rambler or split-level, if the fiber hasn't crushed and the color doesn't bother you, that's the cheaper call.
What do carpeted stairs run in Arlington?

Stair installation starts at $18 per step, done waterfall or cap-and-band style. A typical straight staircase usually totals somewhere in the $235–$400 range depending on the carpet you choose. Landings and pie-shaped winders are measured and priced in the written quote from the start, so nothing gets added on afterward.
How long will my carpet installation take?

One day handles most Arlington houses. Three or four rooms plus a staircase is a normal day's work for the crew; a whole house with heavy furniture or extra stairs can carry into a second day. The timeline is written on your quote, so you know before we start.
Do you move the furniture, or is that on me?

We handle the big pieces. Beds, dressers, couches and tables are included on most jobs, and everything goes back where it stood. Your part is the small stuff — closet floors, electronics, breakables and anything else you'd rather move with your own hands.
Should I stretch my carpet or start over with new?

Four things decide it, and we check them before quoting: whether traffic lanes are flattened, whether seams have opened, whether the backing has gone brittle, and whether pet smell survived a professional cleaning. Any one of those means replacement. In plenty of Gleneagle and Smokey Point houses none of them apply — the carpet is only loose and rippled — and that's a $99-per-room stretch.
Which Arlington neighborhoods does OC Flooring cover?

All of them — old town around Olympic Avenue, Gleneagle, Kent Prairie, Arlington Heights, Sisco Heights and the newer subdivisions out toward Smokey Point and 172nd. The van also runs regularly to Marysville, Stanwood, Silvana, Bryant, Trafton, Granite Falls, Lake Stevens and the rest of north Snohomish County.
What carpet holds up best with dogs and cats?

Around here the problem is mud as often as accidents — dogs off a wet acre, boots off the same. The build is identical either way: a moisture-barrier pad below, sealed-backed solution-dyed nylon above. Nothing reaches the subfloor, where odor turns permanent, and the color is locked into the fiber itself, so diluted bleach won't fade it. The barrier pad runs $0.65 per square foot and up, and pet-focused samples ride along on every visit.
What warranty comes with the install?

Pad first, since that's the piece people miss: some mills void coverage when their carpet sits on the wrong grade of pad, which is why all three ride along in the van. It comes up most on Smokey Point starter homes still running their original builder pad. Otherwise: the mill covers wear and stain, usually 10 to 25 years by grade, and OC Flooring's 1-year workmanship warranty covers the install. Both print on your written quote.
